title: What is Jasper AI? And how to use it
summary: Learn how Jasper works, who it's for, and how it's priced, so you can gauge whether it makes sense for your marketing team.
body_markdown:
Jasper was inescapable in the early years of the AI boom. With its quirky robot logo and "Boss Mode," a tool that churned out long-form blog posts, it had more name recognition than any other[AI writing assistant](https://zapier.com/blog/best-ai-writing-generator/) .


Then[ChatGPT](https://zapier.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt/) came out and changed everything. For consumers, Jasper appeared to fall off the map entirely. (As one user[commented](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5AG9MqFa3Pw&t=208s) on one of Jasper's YouTube videos, "Jasper is still alive? I loved it back in the day before ChatGPT, but now what's the point?")


Jasper is very much alive, but it's been entirely repositioned. It's now an enterprise AI platform that helps marketing teams scale their content while staying on brand.


I've spent a lot of time testing and using Jasper, and here, I'll explain how Jasper works, who it's for, and how it's priced, so you can gauge whether it makes sense for your marketing team.

## Who is Jasper for?


Jasper is designed for mid-market and enterprise brands. Brand consistency, content scaling, and agentic workflows are at its core, and those things matter far more when you're trying to run a large marketing program.


If you're a solopreneur or SMB and you want to sign up for Jasper, you can. But that's not really who Jasper is for. You'll see the first clue during onboarding, where the minimum company size you can select is "200 employees and below."


To get a bit more concrete, here are a few customers Jasper highlights on its website:


-


A 20,000-person trucking company


-


A 3,000-person healthcare vendor


-


A 6,500-person enterprise IT software company


-


An 800-person trade show and events organizer


-


A 1,500-person nonprofit software vendor


-


A 9,500-person media company


-


A 250-person credit union


What all of these businesses have in common is the need to scale marketing content while staying on brand across multiple teams (like performance marketing, social media, content marketing, and PR) and contributors.


## How Jasper works


The three pillars of Jasper are Jasper IQ, Content Pipelines, and Agents. Here, I'll take you through each one, along with some other features worth knowing about.


### Jasper IQ


The heart of Jasper is **Jasper IQ** , a central brand hub that governs every piece of content you create. When you see Jasper's website talk about "strengthening brand control" and an "AI context layer," this is what it's referring to—instead of getting an AI that hallucinates details about your brand, Jasper pulls from here.


Jasper IQ includes:


-


**Brand Voice** : Manage multiple brand voices and keep them consistent across audiences, geographies, and languages.


-


**Audiences** : Adjust your positioning, value propositions, technical language, and CTAs for different target demographics.


-


**Products** : Define product specs, claims, disclaimers, proof points, and pricing.


-


**Style Guides** : Set preferences for Oxford commas, em dashes, abbreviations, and so forth.


-


**Knowledge Base** : Add files manually or sync entire folders from Google Drive or SharePoint.


-


**Visual Guidelines** : Automatically catch off-brand images and flag what needs to change.


Setting all this up is easier than you might imagine. Brand voices and audience profiles are generated automatically after you answer a few questions. For your style guides, knowledge base, and visual guidelines, you'll mainly be copying and pasting the guidelines you already have (or connecting Jasper to company context that's stored elsewhere). Product information is streamlined too: Jasper scans your website URL, knowledge base, or uploaded CSVs.


Once you've imported everything, you'll have a centralized repository of brand and audience guidelines. For example, if you discover that your ideal customer's most compelling buying trigger is different from what you thought, or that certain language resonates with them, you can just update your audience—and moving forward, any content your team creates will take that into account.


Image source:[Jasper](https://www.jasper.ai/product-iq)


Basically, the more you're juggling, the more useful Jasper becomes. If you run an eCommerce brand, for example, you're dealing with a variety of products, multiple audiences, and lots of content formats. And on top of all that, the person handling your social media ads probably isn't the same person who writes your website copy. Jasper keeps your brand consistent across all those variables.


### Jasper Chat


Once you've set up your brand, company information, and product details, you can start creating marketing assets. **Jasper Chat** , an AI marketing assistant, is where you'll go for one-off tasks. Since Jasper IQ is integrated here, you can manually select the brand voice, audience, and language, along with any relevant products and knowledge base context.


There's also an option called "Auto IQ," which attempts to guess the content settings and context you need. It comes with assertive guardrails: in my testing, it assumed I wouldn't want to create water bottle ads for my only audience profile—solopreneurs—because "it sounds more like a business-owner persona than a consumer audience for a bottle ad." (Fair point, honestly.)


Once you're ready to make detailed changes manually, you can switch to Jasper's built-in rich text editor. In addition to standard text changes, you can leave comments, rewrite the asset in a new brand voice, repurpose it for a different audience, or run it through a plagiarism checker.


### Jasper Canvas


**Jasper Canvas** stores all your individually generated assets for a given project. You can organize your content visually, making it easy to quickly scroll through your project's ad copy, landing page copy, and images.


Canvas is where Jasper is most obviously a cross-functional collaboration tool. Performance marketers, content marketers, brand managers, social media managers, PR managers, and lifecycle marketers all organize their assets within a single infinite canvas for each project. Marketing leaders can quickly skim through the assets (rather than just relying on Gantt chart updates) to make sure projects are developing in the right direction.


Image source:[Jasper](https://www.jasper.ai/content-pipelines)


You can also toggle to a table mode, which is useful for sorting project assets by *Owner* , *Section* , *Status* , or *Last Updated* .


### Jasper Agents


Jasper offers 100+ marketing agents known as "task agents." It's important to differentiate these from autonomous marketing agents, which Jasper also has a few of, and which—confusingly—are also called "agents." Jasper's task agents mostly handle assets that can be created with a single prompt, like Instagram captions, product descriptions, and images.


Still, Jasper's task agents offer useful guardrails when you're creating content at scale, making it more likely you'll get the output and formatting you're looking for. (More on that in the next section.)


On Jasper's Business plan—which I wasn't able to test since it's enterprise-only—you get access to a handful of more powerful agents that handle long-running, multi-step tasks like optimization, research, and translation. And if you have any processes that aren't covered by Jasper's prebuilt agents, you can also create your own with **Jasper Studio** .


### Jasper Content Pipelines


If you're creating content at scale, this is where it all comes together.


**Jasper Grid** is an[Airtable](https://zapier.com/blog/what-is-airtable/) -style database built for content workflows. Each row gets its own attributes: you can use text or pull from preset Jasper IQ variables like audience, brand voice, or product details. Each column represents a form of content you want to produce, with Jasper Agents (like the Facebook Ad Agent or Translation Agent) providing field-level guardrails.


Once it's set up, you can create new content by simply clicking the appropriate cell. Or, you can click "Run all" to generate content for your entire project at once.


Image source:[Jasper](https://www.jasper.ai/grid)


You can scale the creation of on-brand visuals with Jasper's Image Pipelines, which run operations like background removal, upscaling, and alt text generation across hundreds or thousands of images. The only catch is that you'll need to set this up through Jasper's API. While that makes it a bit more technical, it's better than the alternative of manually uploading, downloading, or transferring thousands of files as part of your editing process.


### GEO Hub & AI Search Optimization


One of Jasper's newest features is its GEO Hub, which aims to help you show up in[AI chatbots](https://zapier.com/blog/best-ai-chatbot/) (like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude) and[AI search engines](https://zapier.com/blog/best-ai-search-engine/) (like Perplexity and[Google AI Overviews](https://zapier.com/blog/google-ai-overviews/) ).


There are a few components to this:


-


Monitoring your brand presence, sentiment, and citations across AI platforms.


-


Decision Intelligence, which ranks opportunities and recommends what to do next.


-


GEO Agent, which can act on those recommendations autonomously to optimize content and create new content.


-


Measuring results, and feeding that data back into the system for the next initiative.


On a practical level, it looks a lot like the rest of Jasper's platform in the sense that you're interacting conversationally. To kick things off, the GEO Agent includes common starting points like "analyze your brand's visibility" or "identify content gaps."


Image source:[Jasper](https://www.jasper.ai/blog/geo-agent-and-geo-hub)


## Jasper connects with thousands of apps via Zapier


Jasper connects natively with around 15 apps, including Semrush, Salesforce, Google Drive, Slack, and Asana. For anything you need outside of that scope, just[connect Jasper to Zapier](https://zapier.com/apps/jasper/integrations) . ## How much does Jasper cost?


Jasper offers two plans: Pro and Business.


-


The **Pro** plan starts at $69/month ($59/month when billed annually). You get one seat, two brand voices, three audiences, and five knowledge assets, plus access to Jasper IQ, Chat, Canvas, and 100+ agents.


-


The **Business** plan is custom-priced and includes access to Jasper's full platform. You can design custom agents, use Grid to create content pipelines, and add as many Jasper IQ brand voices, audiences, and knowledge assets as necessary. You also get team management features, admin controls, API access, a customer success manager, and access to the GEO Hub for AI search optimization.


You can sign up for a seven-day free trial of the Pro plan. You won't be able to test team features or create content pipelines, but you'll get a good sense for what it's like to create on-brand assets with Jasper and organize them on Canvas.


## Should you use Jasper?


If you're responsible for marketing at a mid-market or enterprise company, Jasper is probably worth your consideration, especially if you currently rely on manually enforcing brand standards.


With Jasper, everything your team produces runs through your style guide and brand standards, so there's no need to run a separate check for brand-friendliness afterwards. When assets (like images) are uploaded that *don't* meet your brand standards, Jasper flags them for replacement automatically.


Jasper's agentic content pipelines are the other big benefit. Marketers can design systems to create content at scale, which is especially effective for routine (but time-consuming) content like product descriptions, social posts, newsletters, ad copy, and translations.


If you're a solo marketer or you run a small team, Jasper isn't built for you. Other[AI marketing agents](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-agents-for-marketing/) and automation platforms are a better fit. But if you're managing dozens (or hundreds) of marketing collaborators, Jasper has real potential to help you stay on brand, boost your team's output, and give you far more visibility over what's happening as each campaign comes together.
